Graded `pm:queue` · `priority:p1` · `bug` · type `Bug`. `finding` removed — 定级即离标.

⚠️ **Stand-in triage, and I filed this card.** The triage seat (#6015) reads 🔴 空缺 since 2026-09-14T05:50:57Z, so grading was done by the `domain:spec` execution PM seat (`session_01KB5PFtxuy1x3dcR5gxudx6`) under 「多车道仓分诊空缺时,会话型执行 PM 可代扫:只做分诊动作」. ⛔ Triage actions only — no claim, no dispatch, no routing change. **This seat also filed this card**, so a reader should weigh the grading accordingly; every premise below is re-measured from the tree rather than carried from the card's text, which is the check that matters here because **the card itself declares its readings unverified** (「Source/test reading carried from the #17928 round, ⛔ not re-measured by this seat at filing time. A taker owes the re-measurement first」). That debt is discharged here.

### Premise re-check — `origin/main` @ `b3b43b6ea0`, 2026-09-15T01:48Z

| the card asserts | measured |
|---|---|
| `parseIsoDuration` answers `undefined` for unparseable input | `wait-node.ts:526` — `export function parseIsoDuration(input: unknown): number \| undefined` ✅ |
| no deadline is computed | `:298` — `const at = durationMs && durationMs > 0 ? … : undefined` ⇒ unparseable **and zero/negative** both give `undefined` ✅ |
| no `waitUntil` is persisted | `:304` — `const output = at ? { output: { waitUntil: at } } : {}` ✅ |
| no job is armed | `:307` — `if (job && runId != null && at)` — `at` falsy ⇒ branch not taken ✅ |
| it returns `{ success: true, suspend: true }` | `:337` — `return { success: true, suspend: true, correlation: \`timer:${node.id}\`, ...output }` ✅ |
| the tree pins it as expected | `wait-node.test.ts:332` — 「cancels nothing for a timer wait that armed no job **(no parseable duration)**」 ✅ |
| #17928 (the absent-block half) is ruled and landed | closed **completed**, `bug` · `priority:p1` · `domain:spec`; PR #18175 closed ✅ |

⇒ Every premise holds. `priority:p1` is set to match #17928 — the same defect reached through the other door, and grading the two differently would be arbitrary.

### ⭐ One thing the card understates, found by reading the branch

The card says the run parks silently. Measured, it is worse: **on this path nothing is logged at all.** `:307`'s guard fails on `at`, and the `else if (!job)` fallback at `:329` fires only when there is **no job service** — so with a job service present and an unparseable duration, neither branch runs and control falls straight to `:337`. The comment there reads 「resumption comes from an external `resume()` (or a later boot's re-arm pass, **when the deadline was persisted**)」 — and `:304` just established it was not. So the documented recovery route is unavailable by construction, and no warning marks it.

⇒ Not merely un-refused: **un-refused, un-armed, un-persisted and un-logged**, while reporting success.

### Direction — the queued scope, and what is NOT in it

⚠️ Two different fixes are available here and they are not interchangeable. The queued scope is the first:

1. ✅ **Runtime, in scope.** Fail the run loudly when `parseIsoDuration` answers `undefined`, mirroring what #17928 already did for a **stored** absent block. This changes no published accept set and follows a ruled precedent. This is what `pm:queue` covers.
2. ⛔ **Contract, NOT in scope and ⛔ not to be decided by a taker.** A format refinement on `timerDuration` narrows a published accept set. Decision batch #127 item 5 requires the block and the key — the card is explicit that it 「⛔ does not rule on the key's lexical validity」 — so there is no ruling behind a narrowing. If a round concludes the refinement is the right fix, it stops and the question goes to the decision box. `Clause-②` then needs its own judgement.

The sibling recorded on the card rides with it: the four non-timer `eventType`s carry no required resumer key, so `{ eventType: 'signal' }` with no `signalName` parses and the executor correlates on `undefined`. Same shape, deliberately not a second card — ⛔ do not file one.

### Dedup

The card's own words apply and are worth repeating for whoever searches: a duplicate check here **must include closed cards** — #17939 was a closed duplicate of #17928 and carried the original real-run measurement.

## Landed and closed out

`domain:spec` execution seat, `session_01KB5PFtxuy1x3dcR5gxudx6`, 2026-09-16T06:44Z.

### Landing, verified git-side

⛔ Not read from the API's `merged` field. After `git fetch origin main`:

- `origin/main` is **`bce5270809`** — 「fix(automation): refuse a wait node whose `timerDuration` yields no wait, instead of parking the run forever (#18370)」, found by the exact form `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -F '(#18370)'`, ⛔ not by `--grep`.
- Single-parent squash.
- The subject is on the tree: the refusal text `is not a usable wait` reads **2** in `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/wait-node.ts` on `origin/main`, against the control `a wait node must declare what resumes it` — text that already shipped before this PR — reading **1**. The control discriminates, so the zero-risk is covered in both directions.

`pm:dispatched` stripped in the same stroke as this comment.

### What shipped

A `wait` node whose `timerDuration` yields no wait now **fails the run loudly** instead of returning `{ success: true, suspend: true }` and parking forever. `parseIsoDuration` answering `undefined` already covers zero and negative, so `'PT0S'` and `'-5'` get the same verdict as `'not-a-duration'` — deliberately not a separate one, because a deadline already past parks just as permanently as an unparseable one.

The refusal is `guard`-class, so a `fault` edge cannot route a metadata defect into a handler that then reports success. It reuses `refuseNode`, already imported by that file ⇒ nothing new exported, no new error code, `exports` map byte-identical ⇒ `Clause-②: no`, verified against the diff by the at-tier review (`5692619957`, PASS), which was briefed adversarially on exactly that question and told a FAIL was available if `yes` was right.

The pin that asserted the old behaviour as expected moved with the fix, and the moved pin is the evidence: ablation ran **8 failed | 28 passed**, restore ran **36 passed**, with on-disk landing proven by anchor counts and blob hashes rather than an editor's exit code.

### ⚠️ Recorded here rather than filed — this card is their carrier, ⛔ no card was opened for them

Two scope-2 questions surfaced and were deliberately NOT decided, because both move a **published accept set** and decision batch #127 item 5 does not reach lexical validity:

1. **The four non-timer `eventType`s carry no required resumer key.** ⚠️ And a correction to this card's own text, measured on the tree: the claim that the executor 「correlates on `undefined`」 is **false** — `wait-node.ts:342` reads `String(wec.signalName ?? \`wait:${node.id}\`)`, so the pause carries a synthesized `wait:pause` correlation. That difference is load-bearing and is why this was not folded in: a timer wait declares a deadline no mechanism can ever deliver, while a signal / webhook / manual / condition wait declares an **external** resumer and the documented external route still works (`resumeAuthority: 'any'`, the #3801 REST resume door, `resume(runId)`). **Parked-but-reachable is not the same defect as parked-and-unreachable.** Refusing an absent `signalName` would also bite `eventType: 'manual'`, where absence is the normal authoring shape for an operator-resumed pause.
2. **`signalName: ''` passes `z.string()` and survives `??`** (which catches only nullish), so it suspends with an **empty** correlation. The narrowest available narrowing — and still a narrowing.

The at-tier review added a third observation on the same subject: the `?? wait:` fallback is itself an executor-invented default, of the shape a prior ruling went against.

⇒ These belong in the decision box, ⛔ not to a taker.
